shots.spoken: Everyone knows Zeus. Ask a room who his brothers and sisters are and the room goes quiet.

shots.spoken: Hesiod names six in one breath. Hestia, Demeter, Hera, Hades, Poseidon, Zeus. Each of them took a piece of the world.
shots.prompt: Six adult gods in a row, eldest to youngest left to right, hearth, grain, crown, dark helm, wave, and a younger sky king, same clothes language, no Roman names on the picture.

shots.spoken: Most people cannot name them. Can you? Five minutes. The line is in the Theogony.

She pours a thin libation toward the fire. No armor, no jewelry crown, no other people. Warm dark ground, clay walls, one doorway into night.

shots.spoken: Zeus was supposed to be swallowed. That is how his father solved a prophecy. Five children already gone. Then his mother handed the king a stone.

Four stone columns, dark warm floor. Old bearded king sits on a stone seat in a long red cloak and cream tunic, empty hands. Empty stone seats beside him. No armor, no modern clothes, no food.

shots.spoken: Kronos had it from Earth and Sky. A son of his would take the throne. He had already done that to his own father. So as each child reached Rhea's knees, he ate it. Whole.

A woman in long rust draped cloth stands alone, head bowed, barefoot. Bare room, stone floor, two columns. No pots, no bowls, no plants, no furniture, no cactus, no modern clothes.

shots.spoken: They sent her to Crete. At night. Gaia hid the sixth baby in a cave on a wooded mountain. The next king of the gods started life in a hole in the ground. With his grandmother.

shots.spoken: Rhea went home with a rock in swaddling clothes. Kronos pushed it down. Hesiod says he did not notice. The son was already growing.
shots.prompt: Flat poster illustration, simple geometric shapes, cream rust terracotta navy. A woman in long cream draped cloth holds a rough grey stone in both hands against her chest. Ancient Greek night hall, two columns. The grey stone is large and obvious. No bowl, no pot, no baby, no planet.

shots.spoken: When Zeus came back, the stone came up first. He set it in the ground at Pytho, under Parnassos. The first monument in Greek myth is a rock a god was fooled into swallowing. Can you name the five he saved?
shots.prompt: Flat poster illustration, simple geometric shapes, cream rust terracotta navy. Brown Greek hills at night. Tiny stars only, no moon, no planets, no orbs, no spheres. A rough grey standing stone planted in the dirt as a marker. Two cypress trees. No temple, no columns, no building, no person, no desert dunes.

shots.spoken: Zeus married Metis first. Hesiod says she was the wisest among gods and among men. She was about to bear a daughter equal to him, and after that a son who would be king of gods and men.

shots.spoken: Earth and Sky told him so, the same two who had warned his father.

No sky visible through the columns, only dark wall. One oil lamp at the left edge. Tall portrait crop, the king larger in the frame than the two advisors, grave and still.

shots.spoken: Kronos had swallowed his children to stop that prophecy, and Zeus had overthrown him for it. Then Zeus sat on the same seat and did the same thing.

Warm dark floor, one oil lamp on the left, long quiet shadows. Tall portrait crop, the empty seats take the left half of the frame, the king the right. Lonely, still, no feast.

shots.spoken: He tricked Metis with soft words and put her in his belly, so no son of hers would ever take the throne. She stays there. Hesiod's line is that she thinks for him now, for good and for evil.
shots.prompt: Gouache illustration with bold dark contour, like a cleaned-up Attic vase painting. Night interior, close enough to read two faces. A woman in a cream chiton stands at the left, three-quarter view, offering both open hands toward a seated bearded king. The king sits at the right in a rust cloak, leaning slightly forward, both hands raised to receive hers, mouth closed. One oil lamp behind them. No food, no wound, no open belly. Tall portrait crop at the waist, the space between their hands is the center of the picture. Intimate and wrong.

shots.spoken: The son never arrives. The daughter does: Athena comes out of his head. The man who escaped being eaten became the father who eats.
shots.prompt: Gouache illustration with bold dark contour, like a cleaned-up Attic vase painting. Night interior, two columns, warm dark floor. A younger woman stands behind and above his right shoulder, three-quarter view, cream chiton, a plain bronze helm, empty hands, no spear, no shield, grey eyes looking out. One oil lamp on the left. Tall portrait crop. She is the new thing in the room.
